scenario: [LEXP.3.7.4]: a `bits`, `sign_extend` or `swap_bytes` call whose run-time arguments lie outside [LEXP.3.7.3]'s domain raises a ComputationError of kind DOMAIN and abandons the activation, as a negative shift count does. One fact carries every argument as an `Int` slot, so the compiler sees no constant and refuses nothing ([LEXP.3.7.4]'s second paragraph). Five rules each make one call outside the domain in their `where`: `bits_negative_lo`, `x.bits(-1, 8)` (lo < 0); `bits_past_bit_63`, `x.bits(60, 5)` (lo + w > 64); `bits_zero_width`, `x.bits(0, 0)` (w < 1); `sign_extend_65` (w > 64); `swap_bytes_24` (w not 16, 32 or 64). None of the five fires. Each fault is raised while matching, at its rule's own join node, so its fault fact names the node (`$beta_<id>`, [LERR.9.11]) and not the rule; rule `on_fault` logs every ComputationError's kind ([LERR.9.1]), five DOMAIN lines in all, and any other kind would show. A builtin that masked or clamped an argument would fire its rule and log one DOMAIN line fewer. PATH PINNED: the domain checks of FN_BITS, FN_SIGN_EXTEND and FN_SWAP_BYTES in libds (`builtins.c`) and Mercury (`ds.eval`).
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    id: String key
    x: Int mutable
    neg: Int mutable
    w0: Int mutable
    five: Int mutable
    eight: Int mutable
    sixty: Int mutable
    w24: Int mutable
    w65: Int mutable

rule bits_negative_lo:
    T t where t.x.bits(t.neg, t.eight) == 0
->
    log info "bits_negative_lo"

rule bits_past_bit_63:
    T t where t.x.bits(t.sixty, t.five) == 0
->
    log info "bits_past_bit_63"

rule bits_zero_width:
    T t where t.x.bits(t.w0, t.w0) == 0
->
    log info "bits_zero_width"

rule sign_extend_65:
    T t where t.x.sign_extend(t.w65) == 0
->
    log info "sign_extend_65"

rule swap_bytes_24:
    T t where t.x.swap_bytes(t.w24) == 0
->
    log info "swap_bytes_24"

rule on_fault:
    ComputationError e
->
    log critical "{e.kind}"
